page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2g.16xlarge belongs to the Local SSDs instance family, configured for data-intensive applications requiring substantial direct-attached solid-state capacity. It is powered by a dedicated 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, offering 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity totals 256.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes 7679 GB of integrated local SSD storage, operates without discrete GPU hardware, and provides a baseline network throughput of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a clear divergence between single-threaded and parallel processing capabilities. Single-core performance falls into lower percentiles, with stress-ng single-core (1108.58) and Geekbench single-core (966.0) scoring in the bottom 25%, alongside poor single-threaded gzip compression at 18.97 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput achieves mid-tier marks across stress-ng multi-core (46759.09), Geekbench multi-core (9986.0), and PassMark CPU (38203.37). In memory and I/O tasks, the instance delivers 118.82 GB/sec in large-block uncached memory read bandwidth, 43.96 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, and 23.86 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Cost efficiency stems from the aggregation of high-density local SSD storage alongside 64 dedicated compute threads, avoiding external storage overhead for high-IOPS operations. The primary performance tradeoff is modest per-core throughput, which makes the instance less effective for latency-critical single-threaded execution or rapid LLM token generation. The hardware configuration aligns with distributed databases, caching clusters, big data processing pipelines, web serving fleets, and search indexing platforms that can exploit wide parallelism and high local storage capacity.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2g.16xlarge is a local-storage-oriented instance within the Local SSDs family, designed for high-capacity I/O and parallel data processing. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor with 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs at 2.5 GHz. The platform provides 256.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, alongside 7679 GB of bundled local SSD storage and a 10 Gbps baseline network interface. It includes no discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate average multi-core and memory throughput, such as a PassMark CPU score of 38203.37 and 43.96 million Redis SET operations per second, contrasted with weaker single-core performance metrics in Geekbench and compression tests. This resource balance delivers cost efficiency for input/output-intensive workloads by eliminating remote storage latency. The instance fits distributed databases, caching clusters, data indexing, and parallel web serving pipelines.
